name: IEC NOT element (rectangular form)
summary: Single-input IEC box marked 1 with a negation at the output, inverting the logic state.
description: The IEC inverter is a single-input element carrying the qualifier 1, meaning the one input must be active, together with a negation at the output. The result is that the output is active when the input is inactive. Data books often replace the circle with a polarity triangle to show an active-low output.

Because negation can be drawn directly on any input or output, a standalone NOT box is often only used where an inverter really exists as a component or as a separate program instruction. On purely functional logic sheets drafters usually fold the inversion into the next element as a negated input.
The symbol gives no information about input thresholds. A Schmitt-trigger inverter adds the hysteresis qualifier; without it, slow or noisy inputs may not be handled cleanly.
readingNotes: Check whether the inversion is a real component or only a notation choice.
Look for a hysteresis mark if the input comes from a slow signal.
drawingChecklist: Mark the box with 1 and negate the output.
Avoid stacking inverters when a negated input would do.
Reference the device when the inverter is a discrete part.
distinction: A box marked 1 without output negation is a non-inverting buffer.
